currentRegisterRecord.RequiredArtifact: A production payload-protection engine behind the existing EventStore hooks, applied field-level to a `ProtectedContent` envelope so every other event field stays plaintext and a destroyed-key field unprotects as the typed value `Erased` without breaking replay: one data-encryption key per `AgentInteraction`, plus an explicit provider-neutral `TargetProtectionKeyAlias` that lets a target-limited creation-outbox `ProtectedContent` field owned by `ConversationAgentState` select that exact interaction DEK without deriving it from the directory aggregate identity, wrapped by a per-tenant key-encryption key custodied through `EXT-SECRETS-1`. The custodian exposes `WrapDek`, `UnwrapDek`, `PinDek`, `UnpinDek`, per-key `DestroyDek`, and an atomic `DestroyDekManifest(BatchId, ManifestDigest, SortedTenantInteractionAliasTargets, GuardCapability)` operation. The batch identity and signed capability are deterministic and target-bound. The capability is non-expiring and revocable, carries its signing-key version, and that version remains verifiable for the full retention of the batch identity and terminal outcome, including exact retry/lookup after consumption or revocation; there is no expiry or renewal path and restore reuses the same identity. Consumption is single-use and all-or-none, returns an ordered irreversible per-target receipt vector, exact retry/lookup returns that vector, a changed target/digest conflicts, and `BlockDeletionBatchConsumption` races `ReserveAndConsumeDeletionBatch` at the same protection owner so exactly one wins. Each first previously uncovered complete protection target `(TenantId, AgentInteractionId, TargetProtectionKeyAlias)` uses one guard-issued batch for its ProtectionFence-assigned monotonic containment ordinal and immutable singleton target manifest; later violation resources for that same target receive coverage links only, no ProtectionFence event alone is a guard capability, and distinct uncovered targets receive distinct ordinals/batches. Hold pinning rejects both per-key and manifest destruction; sealed envelopes remain sealed on broker/read models, `PayloadUnprotectionOutcome` is unreadable after erasure, and snapshot/replay caches inherit the DEK (AD-22, AD-27). The shipped no-op default is not acceptable for content-bearing workflows (AD-14).

It must seal the directory creation-outbox field through the target alias and exercise a multi-interaction `DestroyDekManifest`: deterministic single-use batch identity, exact sorted target binding, all targets destroyed or none, ordered per-key receipts, byte-identical retry and lost-result lookup, changed-manifest conflict, duplicate-consumption denial with exact prior result, hold-pin rejection, and a protection-owner `BlockDeletionBatchConsumption`-versus-`ReserveAndConsumeDeletionBatch` race with exactly one winner, plus capability non-expiry across delayed dispatch/restore and signing-key verification until terminal batch state. A containment batch is accepted only with the exact guard-issued capability for its ProtectionFence-assigned singleton ordinal/manifest; response loss uses exact issuance and protection lookup, exact duplicates reuse it, concurrent distinct targets remain distinct, and containment ordinals cannot reuse the accepted-set batch. Replay must yield typed `Erased` from both source outbox and target events. Negative fixtures cover cross-tenant alias substitution, changed payload/manifest, partial-provider failure, snapshot/cache replay, backup, restore, and stale or revoked guard capability. Command: `TBD`.

**Required v21 manifest-destruction extension:** The engine verifies the complete `DeletionBatchCapabilityV1` JWS against the committed anchor/audience and performs a linearizable exact `GovernanceScopeGuard` lookup at consumption; signature-only or batch-issue-only acceptance is forbidden. The lookup must confirm the same batch/manifest, one active unrevoked attestation, and an exact `DeletionBatchDispatchAuthorized` receipt whose conditional guard commit ordered every earlier post-start hold or compromise before dispatch. Open/missing/mismatched/hold-allowed evidence that preceded dispatch, a stale dispatch, unavailable lookup, or compromised/replaced attestation performs no destruction. A later hold ordered after successful dispatch cannot cancel the possibly begun batch but remains restrictive for other batches, purge, and completion. Emergency key revocation blocks the old attestation before consume; same-batch re-attestation is accepted only after the guard atomically makes it the sole active credential and records a successor dispatch authorization. The protection owner indexes terminal destruction by complete `(TenantId, AgentInteractionId, TargetProtectionKeyAlias)`: a later different BatchId for the exact already-destroyed target returns authenticated `AlreadyDestroyedByBatch(OriginalBatchId, OriginalPerTargetReceipt)`, while changed/cross-tenant targets conflict. Same-alias distinct-resource tests before/after original consumption, hold/dispatch/consume ordering, online-lookup races, compromise/re-attestation, lost acknowledgement, and restore are mandatory.

**Required v23 protection-owner extension:** The engine owns the only post-dispatch cancel-versus-consume state machine. It atomically orders `BlockDeletionBatchConsumption` (admission-integrity or registrar-authenticated per-tenant/key-version compromise) against `ReserveAndConsumeDeletionBatch`; only `Unconsumed` may become `ConsumptionReserved`, and that reservation is the irreversible instant for those cancellation reasons. The owner returns authenticated blocked/reserved/consumed/revoked outcomes and exact lookup after loss; a pending/unknown block performs no new effect. `ConsumptionReserved` recovery completes the same all-or-none batch or returns its terminal vector, never a new authorization. Re-attestation begins only from the exact capability-compromise block, remains blocked while the guard replaces the attestation and issues a successor dispatch, and reopens only when `ActivateReattestedDeletionBatch` conditionally consumes those receipts at the same owner while atomically requiring absence of a replacement-key block at the activation identity's expected tenant-key block-set revision. If that key block exists or wins the compare, activation returns `ActivationBlockedByReplacementKeyCompromise(NewKeyVersion, NewRevocationRevision, NewBlockReceiptId)` and leaves/places the batch in that exact new-key `ConsumptionBlocked` state for another same-batch re-attestation; it never clears a global tenant-key block. Admission-integrity blocks never reopen. The target index is complete `(TenantId, AgentInteractionId, TargetProtectionKeyAlias)`: later violation resources use coverage links and never receive another ordinal/batch; `AlreadyDestroyedByBatch` is exact-target defense in depth, not successor authority. Fixtures cover registration arriving before/at/after reserve; a second compromise before replacement, before dispatch, before/at activation, and after activation before reserve; block delivery/mirror loss; exact activation lookup; no false replacement; restore; and tenant/key/attestation/dispatch/revision substitution.

outstandingFindings.locationAndEvidence: Custody.FinishManifestAsync stores the complete prepared Survivors dictionary in every completed Manifests entry. Repeated one-target erasures retain near-duplicate root populations and grow the bounded native head quadratically; the transition archive does not touch these entries.

ManifestAsync admits Pending with null Survivors before FinishManifestAsync adds a second copy of nearly all Targets. SaveAsync enforces the 30 MiB head only after native rotation/rewrap; valid near-capacity heads can become permanently pending before trim.

TransitionAuthority.ApplyAsync rejects TargetBytes above 8 MiB while RecoverableAnchoredState permits 32 MiB. Registry transitions contain the cumulative sealed records, so valid existing carrier states can be rejected well below the upstream bound; moving historical transitions alone does not fix the current snapshot.

ResolveSnapshotEntriesAsync checks geometry/digest first, then sequential ResolveAsync performs complete identity/canonical-reference checks and WrapAsync. A malformed second enrollment passes the first loop and is rejected only after the first root is issued.

RoleService validates canaryBase64 only when present; Recipe builds calls without checking the required value/seed. ExecuteAsync retains operation/call metadata, then NativeDriver.SealAsync registers the source before reading a missing canary/seed. The absent-input zero-effects requirement is violated.

NativeOccurrenceSource.VerifySealedAsync finally disposes then completes its holder with the request token once. It retains no reference on cancellation/refusal/outage, while the existing worker drains only OccurrenceKeyProvider holders; a cleared live-host verifier holder can indefinitely block trim.

Conditional owner execution returns HoldBlocked without owner registration/reservation. RecoverAsync consults only owner originals, so a lost refused-call result has no recoverable original despite the actual retained hold/guard evidence.

Replay/Backup recovery reads the fixed :replay/:backup cells without an admitted call identity. A prior cell can survive a new admitted-but-undispatched call and be returned as that call completion; source/copy binding does not establish which admitted call wrote it.

RecoverableAnchoredState.CommitAsync admits independently before primary pending persistence. TransitionAuthority retains the exclusive admission, but ReadCurrentOriginalAsync returns only Completed; loss before pending persistence leaves no discoverable exact admitted bytes and blocks later different transitions.

The prepared StatefulSet readiness probe checks TCP only. A listening sealed/uninitialized native service satisfies TCP without usable custody. Replace this direct readiness configuration with the authenticated/TLS health-state semantics and test the prepared probe; no cluster apply.

CompleteHolderAsync accepts any public OwnedErasureRootKey whose 32 bytes are zero and whose holder id matches. Its constructor is public and no issued-instance/disposal identity is checked, so a counterfeit zero buffer can retire a still-live original durable holder.

The receiver executes guard mutation/refusal before persisting GuardAttempts. Recovery searches only current guard Receipts when that ERC entry is absent. Refused outcomes are deliberately absent from committed Receipts, so a failure in this interval loses the actual refusal original.

OccurrenceBindings.ResolveAsync awaits FindAsync before testing permanent loss. A thrown former-ERC read is caught by the method-level refusal and bypasses the independently authenticated loss/source-original branch. Native source ResolveAsync already has an independent-first path; the outer binding ordering defeats it.

bind_rejected_replacement_original validates Current and BlockedReplacement but never validates/binds ownerBatches[0].Original. Substitution of its immutable destruction seal passes both constructed rejected-replacement vectors; exact historical owner evidence is therefore unchecked.

The newly supplied TryReplaySnapshotAsync sends every nonmixed carrier to TryUnprotectSnapshotAsync. That path returns Unreadable when the root is erased. The qualification replay driver requires readable typed-Erased state, so the delivered single-root snapshot pass path cannot satisfy retained-ciphertext erased replay.

Removing its independent copy-policy PermitAsync call would leave those suites green; exercise the actual authenticated production reservation/copy-policy adapter.
